title: crews commit against an unbuilt tree; each break blocks every crew
description:
Supervision finding, measured this session across ~6 hours of two-crew work on the elm-effect-rs conformance port.

Every crew break this session was a compile or test failure in work that had NOT been built before commit. Five separate incidents: (1) crates/elm-effect/src/sync.rs:893 wait_timeout returning a tuple assigned to a MutexGuard; (2) crates/elm-effect/tests/port_logic.rs importing elm_effect::data::Record, a module that does not exist in the workspace; (3) the same file missing a use for predicate::is_tuple_of; (4) crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/schema_binary.rs driving effects through Runtime::run in a library crate test target, which broke l2_cause's library_crate_has_no_run invariant and stayed red across a commit; (5) port_logic.rs:349 tuple_of not checking length.

The blast radius is the whole point: these crews share one repo and one target dir, so one crew's unbuilt commit makes 'cargo test -p elm-effect --features schema' fail for BOTH crews, which is each crew's own fence. The supervising agent then has to diagnose the error text and send the fix, because it must not edit reserved files. That round trip is minutes per incident and it compounds: incident (4) stayed red through a commit because nobody ran the crate's own lint test.

The repair is not more discipline, it is a gate. The repo already has a pre-commit guard that blocks an unattributed or unreserved commit, so the mechanism exists and is enforced at the tool. What is missing is a build gate at the same chokepoint: refuse a commit when 'cargo build' for the touched crates is not green.

Scope: one gate check in the pre-commit hook path, run over the packages resolving from the staged paths, plus the crate's own test target only when it already exists and is fast. Do NOT add a whole-workspace cargo build to every commit — that is the current 4-minute full build and it would push crews to bypass the hook.

Verify: run 'timeout 600 cargo build' with a deliberately broken tree (reintroduce the wait_timeout tuple assignment) and assert the commit is refused with a message naming the file and the crate; then fix it and assert the commit passes.
close_reason: done

title: Port optional-params's 9 open behavior rows
description:
Port optional-params's 9 open behavior rows from the Effect v4.0.0 pin.

The Rust surface for this file is the Router slice added by
elm-effect-rs-port-params-collisions-fz2g in crates/elm-effect-unstable/src/http_server.rs,
so this is incremental: extend that router, do not rebuild what passes.

## What to read

- The TypeScript at the pin: ~/.cache/effect-4.0.0/packages/effect/test/http/FindMyWay/optional-params.test.ts
  and the parser it exercises: packages/effect/src/http/FindMyWay/internal/router.ts
  (OPTIONAL_PARAM_REGEXP, the ignoreTrailingSlash / ignoreDuplicateSlashes options).
- The live row list, which is the spec:

      python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/http/FindMyWay/optional-params.test.ts

## Rules from the elm-effect skill's port-module reference

- Carry a row only when its behavior is representable in Rust, and set it to ported
  only after its Rust test was red and then green, naming that test in the rust column.
- A row we will not carry is not-applicable with a reason in the rust column.
- Flip the ledger under a lease: toron reserve acquire, edit conformance/behavior-tests.tsv,
  commit, release. Never hold the lease between batches.

## Done

cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable passes and conformance/rows-port-remaining.py
reports zero open rows for this file.
close_reason: done; commit fde06e49562185074b920a4e7bcc228bda55e851; verdict unit-test-verified; ran sh -c "cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable && python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/http/FindMyWay/optional-params.test.ts" => exit 0, all targets green (http_server target 49 passed 0 failed), rows-port-remaining 'all 9 rows ported or excused'; rows :4 :18 :24 :30 :42 :53 :71 :89 :106 flipped, each naming its Router test. The pin's optional parameter is route expansion, not a matcher feature: on() rewrites :name? into the path with and without the parameter, so /foo/:bar? already owns /foo (that is row :18's collision) and a ? off the last parameter is refused as RouteError::OptionalNotLast rather than read as part of a name. Both halves are validated before either registers, so a refused declaration changes nothing (the pin throws mid-way and keeps the first half). RouterConfig now carries ignore_duplicate_slashes and ignore_trailing_slash, applied to route patterns and request paths alike. Two corrections to the matcher this router inherited, both found by these rows and neither a special case for them: a capture may be empty (the pin slices the segment with no length check, which is what lets /test/hello/:optional capture "" at a trailing slash), and a later capture is tempered by the separator before it rather than lazy (the pin compiles :p1-:p2 to (.*?)\-\-(...), so foo-bar-baz splits foo-bar / baz, not foo / bar-baz). Route order also gained the pin's walk rule that a static segment is tried before a parametric one; without it / lost to /:optional with an empty capture on row :42. Not carried and refused loudly: '*' wildcards (Unsupported) and an unbalanced '(' (Invalid). Not carried, named in the module doc: the case-insensitive option, maxParamLength, '::' and '%' escaping, and real regex evaluation (a '(...)' source compares as the literal it holds, which every one of these nine rows uses). Red first against HEAD: E0432 for RouterConfig plus E0599 for OptionalNotLast and make_with, then green. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain -- the optional flag is a rewrite of the declaration into two routes, which is why the collision, the root case and the slash options all fall out of ordinary registration instead of a new matcher branch. fix-root-causes -- the two matcher rules the rows broke were wrong in the code this bead inherited, so the fix is in the capture semantics (the compiled form the pin actually matches with), not a check bolted onto the failing rows. sequence-verifiable-units -- the nine rows landed as one red-then-green batch over tests/:4 through :106.

title: ManagedRuntime::make swallows a layer's construction failure, and its build scope dies with the call
description:
Both found porting beads against the framework.

## Bug 1 (verified by running a probe): make() discards the failure

ManagedRuntime::make's doc said 'A failing layer surfaces as a defect on the built runtime, matching how this port reports construction failure.' layer.build(&scope).ok() did the opposite: the Cause<E> was dropped and services became None, which is indistinguishable from ManagedRuntime::new(). A services interpreter then reported 'no services' instead of the cause. Verified: a layer whose constructor fails produced context() == None.

Fixed to return Result<Self, Cause<E>>, which is the pin's shape — ManagedRuntime.make there yields an Effect, so construction failure fails the build and the caller cannot ignore it. Only 7 call sites, all tests.

## Bug 2 (latent, fixed as defense): the build scope died with make()

let scope = Scope::new(0); layer.build(&scope).ok(); — the scope was dropped at the end of make, and Scope::drop calls close(), which runs every finalizer registered during the build. Any resource a layer acquired with acquire_release would have been released before the runtime's first effect ran.

Latent today only because Layer::from_factory's constructor is a pure Effect with no scope access, so nothing can register a finalizer there. It becomes load-bearing the moment a scoped constructor form lands, which is the Effect idiom (Layer.scoped). The runtime now owns the scope, so finalizers run when the runtime drops — after Runtime::shutdown has interrupted every live fiber, which is the correct order.

## A third candidate I investigated and REJECTED

A panic in Interpret::interpret ran outside run_effects' catch_unwind and looked like a defect in the fold's own guarantee. I built a probe that proved it: the process panicked and the loop never survived. Then I found crates/elm-effect-elm/tests/loop_joint.rs:596, a #[should_panic] test pinning the opposite contract with its reason in a comment: a panic in the interpreter is a bug in the interpreter and must reach the host rather than become a message. That is the effect-oriented law (a handler for typed failures must not swallow defects), so the pinned behavior is right and my fix was wrong. Reverted, no change. Worth knowing that interpret_in_env inherits the same contract: a panic while wiring the world propagates to the host.

## Fence
sh -c 'cargo test -p elm-effect --lib && cargo test -p elm-effect --test layer && cargo test -p elm-effect-elm --test loop_joint && sh conformance/witness.sh'
close_reason: ManagedRuntime::make now returns Result<Self, Cause<E>> and owns its build scope. Verified: lib (14), layer (9), loop_joint (14), every integration suite, and witness.sh all green.

title: approval drainer: route the inbox decision-scan through run_mail_off_runtime
description:
The approval drainer panics on its inbox scan, so a parked SIGNOFF approval is
never auto-resolved and recovery becomes manual.

The drainer runs on a std thread that builds its own current-thread runtime
(`src/pane.rs:2391-2405`), then calls `mail.inbox(...)` inside it
(`src/pane.rs:2504`) which `block_on`s the shared runtime
(`src/mail_shim.rs:888-893` -> `456-461` `RUNTIME.block_on`). The known fix
`run_mail_off_runtime` (`src/backend/mod.rs:108-118`, landed as
bd-swarm-loop-durable-panic-atlo) was applied to the durable loop and to the
drainer's mailbox *build*, but not to the drainer's inbox scan.
`src/mail_shim.rs:136-158` documents this exact panic naming the drainer as the
caller and guards only `build_mailbox_once` via `Handle::try_current()`;
`mail.inbox` has no guard.

Mechanism proven by the repo's own canaries:
`cargo test --bin flywheel off_runtime_tests` passes both
`inline_shared_runtime_block_on_panics_inside_a_runtime` (the panic reproduces)
and `run_mail_off_runtime_bridges_without_nesting` (the remedy works).

Observed live during the `wave-swarm` compose run on elm-effect-rs at
2026-10-10T22:18:41Z: `thread 'approval-drainer' panicked ... Cannot start a
runtime from within a runtime`, immediately after a parked approval
(`fw-composed-2026-10-10T22:18:41Z.7.0`).

## Scope

The run itself is always safe: `src/main.rs:29134` discards the join error
(`let _ = approval_drainer.join().map_err(...)`), unlike the spawn-drainer
whose panic propagates via `?`. What dies with the thread is the SIGNOFF
auto-pass and the `approve:`/`reject:` token resolve
(`src/pane.rs:2461-2546`); the parked promise then waits for a human
`flywheel workflow approve`. The CLI path still resolves it, so no work is
lost — but the automation that was supposed to end the wave silently stops.

Reachability: requires an in-process backend (no `[mail.toron] url`) AND a
parked approval AND `pass % 13 == 0` (`src/pane.rs:2494-2504`).

title: Port ChildProcessSpawnerTest.ts's portable behavior rows
description:
# Port ChildProcessSpawnerTest.ts's portable behavior rows

## Source
`~/.cache/effect-4.0.0/packages/effect/test/process/ChildProcessSpawnerTest.ts` — 67
`unported` rows for `packages/effect/src/process/ChildProcessSpawner.ts`.

## Rust owner
`crates/elm-effect-unstable/src/process.rs` (372 lines) already lands the surface
these rows drive: `command_array` / `command_template`, `CommandSpec`
(`cwd`/`env`/`clear_env`/`spawn`), `ChildHandle` (`id`/`wait`/`kill`),
`CommandOutput` (`code`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`is_success`/`stdout_text`),
`Pipeline`, `run`, and `ProcessError` (`Spawn`/`NonZeroExit`/`MissingEnv`).

Witness: extend `crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/process_spawn.rs`, one test
per row, each carrying a `// ChildProcessSpawnerTest.ts:<line> — <behavior>`
comment so the flip names the row it proves.

## Method
RED first: write the witness for a row, watch it fail (or watch the capability
be missing), implement only what the row needs, then flip with
`conformance/flip-row.py`.

## Scope boundary
Rows that need capability `process.rs` does not model stay `unported` in this
unit, they are not excused here:
- combined/interspersed `.all` output, incremental stdout streaming
- stdin fed to a child, extra fd plumbing (fd3+, gaps, bidirectional)
- specific-signal kill, force-kill after a timeout, scope-close kill
- `unref` and process-group cleanup (rows carried as `it.skipIf` upstream)

Leaving at least one row open keeps `ChildProcessSpawner.ts` `unmatched`, so this
unit needs **no** `conformance/modules.toml` change. That file is under
CyanGlen's exclusive lease (reason `elm-effect-rs-azf3`); a byte changed there
by anyone else is blocked by the pre-commit guard. A later unit that closes or
excuses the remaining rows takes the lease and flips the derived status.

## Verify
`sh -c "cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable --test process_spawn"`
close_reason: done

# Port the ComprehensiveCli integration rows of the cli completion generators

Source rows: `packages/effect/test/cli/completions/completions.test.ts`, the
`Completions integration` section — `:814` (bash), `:854` (zsh), `:885` (fish).
These are the last 3 unported rows of that file; the other 67 were closed by the
descriptor, bash, zsh and fish units.

## Oracle

The pin's `test/cli/fixtures/ComprehensiveCli.ts` (439 lines) is transcribed into
`crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/completions_fixtures/mod.rs::comprehensive()`.

The goldens under `tests/fixtures/completions/{bash,zsh,fish}/comprehensive.*`
were produced by running the pin's **own** `Command.make` / `Command.withSharedFlags`
/ `Flag` / `Argument` API to build the fixture, then the pin's **own**
`cli/internal/completions/descriptor.ts` + `bash.ts` / `zsh.ts` / `fish.ts` to
generate the scripts. The Rust port matches that output byte for byte, which is
stricter than the pin's `assert.include` rows.

`Command.withSharedFlags` merges the shared flags into both the command's own
config and its context config, so the Rust descriptor sets both `flags` and
`context_flags` the way the pin does.

## Witness

- `crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/cli_completions_bash.rs::generates_valid_bash_script_for_comprehensive_cli` (`:814`)
- `crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/cli_completions_zsh.rs::generates_valid_zsh_script_for_comprehensive_cli` (`:854`)
- `crates/elm-effect-unstable/tests/cli_completions_fish.rs::generates_valid_fish_script_for_comprehensive_cli` (`:885`)

Each mirrors the pin's own assertion set, and `comprehensive` is registered in
the three `*_goldens()` lists so the byte-equality tests cover it too.

## Verify

`cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable --test cli_completions_bash --test cli_completions_zsh --test cli_completions_fish`

## Why no modules.toml change

`completions.test.ts` is linked to no module in `conformance/modules.toml`, so

title: doorbell digest: scope journal and unanswered reads to the requested project
description:
`flywheel doorbell digest <PROJECT>` requires and spell-checks a PROJECT
positional, then discards it and returns every workspace's wakes.

`src/cmd/doorbell.rs:616-618`: `let _ = cfg; let _ = project; let entries =
crate::doorbell::journal_read_all(&crate::config::state_dir());` — plus
`journal_workspaces_list` across all workspaces (lines 622-631). Only
`--identity` scopes the output; the required `<PROJECT>` affects nothing.

Reproduced: `flywheel doorbell digest elm-effect-rs` printed
`UNANSWERED (escalated):` with 18 pins belonging to other projects, and sweep
rows labeled `workspace:flywheel-beads`. On a host carrying seven workspaces,
the command that answers "what did the doorbell hold for my project" returns
all of them.

The practical cost is a misdiagnosis: the digest reads as though elm-effect-rs
had 18 unanswered pins, when the project-scoped
`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/flywheel-elm-effect-rs.unanswered` does not
exist. That is exactly the signal an operator would act on.

title: effect.rs is missing scoped, provideService, withFiber, cached, isEffect and acquireUseRelease, which block Effect.test.ts's first rows
description:
Effect.test.ts has 230 open rows. The first ~16 are excused and cannot be carried
until effect.rs grows these APIs.

## Missing from crates/elm-effect/src/effect.rs

The file has 21 pub fns: succeed, fail, die, interrupt, from_option,
from_result, transpose_option, on_error, ensuring, on_exit, catch,
catch_defect, catch_cause, sync, flat_map, map, result, exit, or_die,
map_err, fail_cause.

Absent, each blocking named rows:
- `scoped`        — Effect.test.ts:79  "scoped closes its scope when interrupted after installing it"
- `provideService` and `withFiber` — :124 "provideService restores the original context if interrupted before its body"
- `cached` and `cachedInvalidateWithTTL` — :155 "never strands a second caller when the owner yields before registering cleanup"
- `isEffect`      — :209 (a TS runtime type guard; in Rust likely Option<&dyn Any> like Cause's and AiError's guards)
- Effectable.Class and asEffect — :215, :226
- acquireUseRelease family — the acquireUseRelease cluster

## Verification

Each row was read, and the API absence confirmed by grep across
crates/elm-effect/src/. The 16 excuses carry 16 DISTINCT reasons naming the
missing function, not one swept reason. The ledger's paired guard is green.

## Why this is the enabler and not busywork

Effect is the crate's core. `scoped` and `provideService` in particular are the
resource-safety pair the rest of the library leans on — Stream, Channel and the
STM surfaces all need a scoped acquire/release, so adding them here likely
unblocks rows in those files too, not just these 16. `isEffect` is cheap: it is
the same Option<&dyn Any> guard shape already used twice in this repo
(cause.rs's five guards and ai.rs's is_ai_error), so it is a copy of an existing
pattern rather than new design.

## Suggested order

1. `isEffect` — existing pattern, ~8 lines, unblocks :209 immediately.
2. `scoped` — the resource-safety primitive, unblocks :79 and gives Stream a
   home for its scoped rows.
3. `provideService` — unblocks :124 and the Context.Service rows.
4. `withFiber`, `cached`, `acquireUseRelease` — larger, do after the above land.

comments.text:
Audit correction + first slice landed (CalmHarbor).

One name at a time, read against the source. Four of the six named APIs are not what the description says.

1. scoped - WAS a real gap, and is now LANDED: Effect::scoped in effect.rs (suspend node that mints a fresh Scope, replaces the ambient scope provision, runs the body, closes the scope on every exit), ScopeTag in scope.rs (service Arc<Scope>), replace_tag in service.rs (innermost wins; insert_tag would poison an already-provisioned scope). Row Effect.test.ts:79 flipped to ported, witness scoped_closes_its_scope_when_interrupted_after_installing_it. Red-then-green: without the API that witness fails to compile (E0432 ScopeTag, E0599 scoped x2), with it l5_scope is 10/10; crate-wide 1276 passing; conformance green.
   Named reduction: interruption is cooperative here, so the row's 'interrupted mid-body' maps to an interrupt cause reaching the run edge. The pin closes the scope from onExitUnsafe while the fiber unwinds; this carrier cannot unwind an effect in flight, and a fiber interrupted while its effect runs reaches Ctx::add_finalizer instead. Platform substitution, recorded here so the row is not read as more than it is.

2. provideService - NOT missing. The capability is Effect::provide / provide_merge / provide_from / provide_reference (service.rs). A pub fn provide_service would be a second name for provide, so the fence's grep for that name could never pass by honest work.

3. withFiber - genuinely absent, and not an effect.rs-only change: nothing exposes the running fiber to a description. Services are per-description and there is no fiber/ctx tag, so it needs a handle provided at the spawn seam (runtime.rs Driver::spawn -> Ctx::new).

4. cached / cachedInvalidateWithTTL - absent as Effect::cached. The machinery it would wrap exists (cache.rs single-flight memo, TTL, waiter rule), so it is a wrapper plus a row carry, not new caching design.

5. isEffect - the description's claim is wrong; row :209 is already not-applicable with a sound reason (whether a value is an Effect is a compile-time fact in Rust). Nothing to build.

6. acquireUseRelease - Effect::acquire_use_release is absent, but rows :315, :342, :370, :2189 and :2209 name delay, uninterruptible, void and runFork alongside it, so building it alone would not carry them. The capability exists at Scope::acquire_release / Ctx::acquire_release, and :2850 is already carried by acquire_use_release_returns_the_usage_result.

title: Schedule + retry/repeat (never retry defects or interrupts)
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 3, "Schedule and the remote stack" (schedule part).

Deliverables:
- `Schedule<In, Out>` as a value: decides whether to continue and how long to
  wait. `recurs(n)` = n retries after the first attempt. `max` continues while
  every member continues, waits the longer delay. `min` continues while any
  member continues, waits the shorter delay. Exponential backoff composed with
  a spaced ceiling, then jitter (from the `Random` service), then a predicate
  (e.g. `error.retryable`).
- `retry` re-runs after typed failure; `repeat` re-runs after success. They are
  different combinators. Defects and interrupts are never retried.
- Tests: `crates/elm-effect/tests/schedule.rs` covering recurs counting,
  max/min composition, jitter drawn from `Random::with_seed`, and
  `retry_never_retries_die_or_interrupt`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect --test schedule
```

---
close_reason: Schedule value with recurs/max/min/exponential/capped/jitter/given delivered; retry re-runs typed failures until policy stops; repeat re-runs successes; defects and interrupts never retried; jitter deterministic per Random seed; max waits longer while all continue, min waits shorter while any continues. PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — retry policy is a value, not a loop; boundary-discipline — retry wraps the smallest idempotent region

title: policy::remote: the L4 order + defaults + bounded waits
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 3, "Schedule and the remote stack" (policy part). Laws L4, L10.

Deliverables:
- `policy::remote(call)` builds the innermost-to-outermost order: filter,
  fallback, cache, budget timeout, retry, circuit breaker, rate limit, bulkhead,
  attempt timeout, call. Defaults, all overridable, none infinite: 3 retries
  after first; backoff 250 ms; ceiling 10 s; full jitter from `Random`;
  attempt timeout 30 s; budget 2 min; bulkhead 8 in flight / queue 32 / wait
  5 s; rate limit none until passed a limiter; breaker closed until passed one
  (open after 5 consecutive typed failures, half-open after 30 s, one probe).
- `BreakerOpen` is a typed error and does NOT count as a retry attempt.
  Unbounded retry is not constructible through `policy::remote`.

  attempt timeout; call returns immediately once admitted; success),

title: Fiber: fork/join/interrupt, interruptibility, supervisor catch_unwind
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 1, "Fibers, interruption, and scope" (fiber part).

Deliverables:
- `Fiber` with id, interruptibility depth, scope stack, context, parent.
- `fork_child` (child dies with parent; parent waits for child finalizers),
  `fork_scoped` (caller-supplied `Scope`), `fork_in`, `fork_detach` (attaches
  to the runtime root scope; NO supervisor parameter).
- Default start is deferred (child begins when the current fiber yields or
  completes); `start_immediately: true`; `uninterruptible: true | inherit`;
  default interruptibility = runtime default (interruptible).
- `join`; `Fiber::interrupt` waits until the target's finalizers finish
  (back-pressure), `Fiber::interrupt_unsafe` does not wait. Default is the
  waiting form. Interruption is delivered at interruptible steps; an
  uninterruptible region runs to completion and the flag fires when depth
  returns to zero.
- Supervisor: the one legal `catch_unwind` in the workspace, living in the
  supervisor module only. A panic stores `Die`; a sibling fiber keeps running;
  the process stays up.
- Tests (land first, red): `panic_in_child_is_die_and_sibling_lives`;
  `fork_detach_child_ends_at_runtime_shutdown` (no supervisor arg);
  `interrupt_waits_for_finalizers`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect panic_in_child_is_die_and_sibling_lives
```

title: Elm: replay, snapshot {model, offset}, middleware, subscriptions
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 8 Redux rules + L12. The durable log lands in wave 12; this
bead's replay works against an in-memory log behind the same trait once wave 12
exists, and against a minimal in-crate log until then (do not fork the trait).

Deliverables:
- Time travel replays the message log from the latest snapshot; the snapshot
  stores the model and the log offset it includes. Default snapshot interval
  every 100 messages, configurable per program. Replay is a pure fold plus a
  comparison of the command lists; it does not re-execute providers (their
  results are already messages).
- Middleware (if written) is `fn(&Msg) -> Msg`, applied before `update`; no
  access to `Cmd`/`Effect`; sagas/thunks/listeners are not representable.
- Subscriptions are a stream of model snapshots (SubscriptionRef underneath);
  the handle cannot send into the model.
- Tests: `fold_is_deterministic` (same log twice), `replay_matches_commands`,
  `snapshot_is_model_plus_offset`.

## VERIFY


title: Journal: plan_park ceiling + pending upsert key
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 9, "Journal" (park part).

Deliverables:
- `plan_park(until_ms, max_wait_secs, now_ms, ceiling)` pure; `ceiling` defaults
  to 86400 s; a wait above ceiling is a TYPED REFUSAL, not a shorter sleep; a
  past `until_ms` is `ResumeNow` reporting the overdue gap without wrapping.
  The host supplies `now_ms`; replay may move park→resume; that movement is the
  point.
- Park persists as a pending row: `upsert_pending` idempotent on
  `(run_id, promise_id, park_generation)`; a second upsert with the same key
  writes nothing. `ResumeNow` builds no intent; `park_intent` builds the value
  before the wait. No effect-row write to `parked`; `Parked` stays parseable
  and non-terminal.
- Tests: `plan_park` (refusal above 86400, no wrap, due-now), 
  `second_pending_upsert_writes_nothing`, `parked_row_is_resumable_not_terminal`.

title: Durable log: DurableLog trait, offset minting, atomic append, seq rules
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 9b, "Durable log". Law L16 (append part). Read
`skills/elm-effect/references/durable-log.md` before coding.

Deliverables:
- `DurableLog` trait in `elm-effect-journal`; first implementation in-process
  (the log IS the stream; it is not a client of the Node server).
- Offsets: opaque, lexicographically ordered, minted by the log; sentinels `-1`
  (start) and `now` (tail) are never minted as real offsets; a hand-built
  offset is rejected.
- Append is atomic (crash leaves the previous offset; a read never returns a
  partial message; JSON mode keeps boundaries). Producer identity is
  `(producer_id, epoch, seq)` all-or-none; a seq that is not `last + 1` and not
  an already accepted seq is rejected. Each JSON message carries the schema
  version; an unknown version is a typed error.
- Tests: `crates/elm-effect-journal/tests/durable_log_append.rs` —
  `hand_built_offset_is_rejected`, `seq_gap_is_rejected`,
  `partial_identity_is_rejected`, `append_is_atomic`,
  `unknown_schema_version_is_typed_error`.

## VERIFY

```bash
cargo test -p elm-effect-journal --test durable_log_append
```

---
close_reason: DurableLog trait with in-process kernel green; minted lexicographic offsets with -1/now sentinels never minted; hand-built offsets rejected; seq gaps rejected with same-triple idempotent replay; unknown schema versions typed. PRINCIPLES: boundary-discipline — the log is a trait; the kernel runs in-process; make-operations-idempotent — same triple appends once

title: Scope + acquire_release: release on every exit, reverse order, once
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 1, "Fibers, interruption, and scope" (scope part). Laws L6, L7.

Deliverables:
- `Scope`, `acquire_release` (finalizer is an effect; runtime runs it), the
  finalizer stack, `Scope::provide` (lends a scope; does not close it).
- L6: success, typed failure, and interruption all release; reverse order of
  acquisition; exactly once; a finalizer failure is APPENDED to the cause and
  never erases the original reason.
- L7: finalizers and marked commit regions are uninterruptible: cancellation
  requested during a release runs it to completion, then takes effect.
- `Drop` of a guard is not the release path for anything needing `.await`;
  sync resources may still use `Drop`.
- Tests (land first, red): `release_on_three_exits` (order `[second, first]`),
  `cancel_during_release_finishes_release`, `finalizer_failure_is_appended`.

title: Runtime + deterministic executor + five outcomes
description:
ADR-0002 Phase 1, "Carrier" (runtime) and the L2 law test. The `Parked`
assertion of L2 lands in the journal wave (phase 9).

Deliverables:
- `Runtime::run` (the edge), `Runtime::run_main` (owns signals and exit codes:
  success 0, typed failure 1, defect 2, interrupt 130), `ManagedRuntime` for a
  non-effect caller.
- `Executor` trait: `spawn_boxed(BoxFuture<'static, ()>)`,
  `spawn_blocking(Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>)`. `TokioExecutor` behind feature
  `tokio` with defaults `worker_threads = 4`, `queue_bound = 4096` (overridable,
  never constants inside combinators).
- `DeterministicExecutor` in `crates/elm-effect-test`: runs one ready fiber at a
  time in registration order; timers complete only when the test clock says so;
  `tokio::time::pause` is not the spec.
- L2 test (lands red before the runtime exists): `five_outcomes_do_not_collapse`
  — builds success, `Fail`, `Die`, `Interrupt` and asserts the classifiers;
  `catch` on the error channel leaves `Die`/`Interrupt` in place;
  `catch_defect` leaves typed failures/interrupts alone; `catch_cause` is the
  only combinator that sees all three and library code does not call it.
- L3 lint target: `library_crate_has_no_run` — `Runtime::run`/`block_on` appear
  only in `elm-effect` itself, `elm-effect-test`, and `examples/` binaries.

title: a rate-limited crew kills loop-mode supervise within three passes
description:
Observed twice this session: flywheel loop-mode supervise elm-effect-rs --work --interval 120 stops itself after 3 consecutive failed passes, and the failing pass is a pass where an agent is merely BLOCKED.

The output is explicit:

    [loop] blocked flywheel-elm-effect-rs-oc
    [loop] --once pass done
    flywheel: loop: agents blocked (on_blocked=continue; pass --on-blocked stop|mail to control)

then, twice more, then

    flywheel: loop-mode supervise stopping after 3 consecutive failed passes

So with on_blocked=continue a blocked agent still yields a FAILED pass, and the supervisor treats three of those as a dead loop and exits. continue is supposed to mean exactly the opposite: keep going despite the block.

The block that triggered it was a PROVIDER RATE LIMIT, not a stuck agent. IcyCoast's pane carries 'Error: Rate limit exceeded. Please try again later.' from the Step 5 Preview Free model. Nothing is wrong with the tree — the fence is green and the other crew is committing — yet supervision dies in about six minutes.

loop-mode run accepts --on-blocked continue|stop|mail, and its mail branch notifies the captain at tiers T0/T1/T2 and only halts at T3 (src/durable.rs:8713). But loop-mode supervise does not forward --on-blocked, so a supervisor can only ever run with continue, which is the one policy that both declines to notify AND counts the block as a failure.

Expected: either supervise forwards --on-blocked (so mail is reachable), or continue stops counting a provider-side block as a failed pass. A rate-limited crew is a reason to wait, not a reason to stop supervising the crews that are still working.

Verify: with one agent deliberately blocked, run flywheel loop-mode supervise elm-effect-rs --work --interval 30 against a scratch project and assert it survives at least five passes, then assert it notifies the captain within one interval.
close_reason: done

title: elm-effect-elm: loop-joint silent drop on append failure + erased typed failure
description:
Takeover of the elm-loop-joint work. CalmHarbor (mail-only pin, no injectable pane, P2 sub-case) landed a green implementation of /tmp/elm-loop-joint.md but left two defects, both in Loop::run_commands:

1. Silent drop: a durable command whose DurableLog append FAILS does \`Err(_) => continue\` — it neither runs nor produces a message, and nothing reaches intents() either. The fold never learns the command was dropped. Requirement 2 of the doc says no silent drop.

2. Erased typed failure: Program::failure is hardwired to Cause<String>, so run_commands renders the interpreter error with to_string(). A program can only string-match (the test does \`failures[0].contains(\"boom\")\`). ADR-0002 L2 says the five outcomes stay apart; collapsing the typed channel into text breaks that.

Fix (both in run_commands, root cause, not per-caller guards):
- classify a non-success cause into a Failure enum (Fail / Defect / Interrupted) and add Program::failure(&Failure) -> Msg so the fold matches on the kind structurally;
- route a rejected append through the same method so the fold sees it, while still not running the command.

Scope: crates/elm-effect-elm/src/lib.rs, tests/loop_joint.rs (new), tests/program.rs, tests/replay.rs (Program impls + assertions only). No edits to crates/elm-effect or crates/elm-effect-journal beyond their public API.

VERIFY
close_reason: Both command-outcome losses fixed in Loop::run_commands: a rejected durable append now reports Failure::NotAppended (and still does not run the command), and every non-success cause classifies into a Failure enum reached through the now-required Program::failure, so fail/defect/interrupt stay structurally apart. 22 tests green in elm-effect-elm incl. interrupt and empty-cause coverage; the shared provider counter's third unlocked writer was fixed too. PRINCIPLES: fix-root-causes — both defects live in run_commands, so both fixes land there instead of per-caller guards; prove-it-works — the unit-test-verified gate row carries sha=a57dc1ce79ee8b4cf07925d7998e7ce82705662e.

title: not-ready alert: fall back from an unresolvable created_by to the configured operator pin
description:
The not-ready alert can never reach a human-created bead's creator, so the one
notification that would explain a stalled wave never lands.

`loop-mode run --work` decides a bead is dispatchable only when
`verify.is_some() && principles_block_reason(b).is_none()` (flywheel
`src/durable.rs:1024-1028`; `src/principles.rs:213-251` requires every P<=2
citation name to be one of the 21 canonical names, else `Incomplete`). When a
bead fails that gate the loop tries to mail the planner, and
`resolve_planner_for_bead` (`src/main.rs:34927-34957`) takes the bead's
`created_by`. `br` derives `created_by` from `$USER`
(`~/workspace/beads/src/config/mod.rs:5802-5809`, `create.rs:686`), so a bead
created by the operator is addressed to an OS username that is never a
registered mail identity. The fallback chain prefers `created_by` over the
configured operator (`cfg.agent_mail.name`) and nothing re-checks that it
resolves.

Measured on this host: `flywheel __ready elm-effect-rs` returns 18 beads, 17
with non-canonical citations (`behavior-parity-is-witnessed` x15,
`static-interpreter-seam` x2) — all 17 not-ready by the gate — and
`toron mail whois elm-effect-rs bangedorrunt` answers
`unknown agent name: bangedorrunt (register first)`. Every alert for every one
of them fails.

The failure is non-fatal by contract (`__mail-not-ready` exits 0 with
`{ok:false,error}`, `src/durable.rs:1223-1225`), but the durable loop prints
`planner mailed: {... "ok": false ...}` — a success-worded line over a failed
send. So beads are silently never dispatched and the reason is silently never
delivered.

comments.author: CoralHarbor
comments.text:
Four defects, all in `crates/elm-effect-schema/src/lib.rs`, which is under BoldKite's exclusive lease, so none is fixed here. Between them they block roughly twenty of this bead's ninety-one open rows.

## A. `intersect` compares `SchemaKind` structurally, so two same-type schemas cannot intersect

```
Schema::<Unknown>::from_json_schema(&serde_json::json!({
    "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
    "allOf": [{"type": "object", "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}}]
}))
```

gives `Err(expected a member intersecting the same base at $.allOf, got a member with a different base)`.

Both sides name `object`, and the pin merges their `properties`. The port refuses because the base's kind is `Record(String, Never)` while the member's is `Struct([...])`. The guard is the `member_kind != base_kind && member_kind != Json` check around lib.rs:3010. The pin's rule is about the JSON Schema *type name*, not about whether the port's own kind datatype is equal.

Object-intersection rows this blocks: 2716, 2738, 2758, 2779, 2817.
Array-intersection rows this blocks: 2420, 2443, 2461, 2479, 2497, 2515, 2532, 2547. Those eight each run the pin's `assertArrayAllOf`, which tries both member orders, so all sixteen of its assertions hit this.

## B. The same guard must answer `never` instead of refusing when the two sides name different types

`{allOf: [{type: "array"}, {type: "string"}]}` must import as `Schema.Never` / `never`; it errors. Same for object-and-string, null-and-string, `{allOf: [false, ...]}`, and `{type: "string", allOf: [{anyOf: [number, boolean]}]}`.

`{allOf: [{"const": 1}, {"const": 2}]}` is a different failure of the same row: it returns `Schema.Literal(2)`, keeping the last value instead of seeing that the two cannot both hold.

Rows: 1776, 2570, 2577, 2584, 2591, 2598, plus 2461, 2515 and 2795, which expect `never` out of a tuple or an object intersection.

## C. `new_kinded` gives every kind except String, Number and Boolean an identity decoder

`rebuild`'s doc comment claims "a rebuilt schema enforces what the schemas it was built from enforced". It does not:

```
{allOf: [{type: "null"}, {type: "null"}]}         -> code Schema.Null        decode(Text("x")) = Ok
{type: "array", allOf: [{description: "a"}]}      -> code Schema.Array(..)   decode(Text("x")) = Ok
```

A plain `{type: "null"}` refuses the string, so the merged form is strictly weaker than either of its inputs. `new_kinded` (lib.rs:526) matches on String, Number and Boolean and falls through to `Schema::new(|value| Ok(value), ...)` for every other kind: Object, Array, Null (which arrives as `Opaque("null")`), Struct, Record, Tuple, Optional, Rest, Check and Json.

Every `allOf` merge into one of those kinds is affected, including rows already marked `ported`, and a repr-only test cannot see it, which is the reason it survived.

## D. The annotation allow-list drops three built-in JSON Schema annotations

The list is `["title", "description", "format"]` at lib.rs:2483, :3336 and :3463.

```
{type: "string", format: "email", contentEncoding: "base64",
 contentMediaType: "application/json", contentSchema: {"type": "number"}}
```

yields `Schema.String.annotate({ "format": "email" })`, where the pin carries all four. Rows 1147 and 2700.

## What landed on this lane

Commit cde2cb1 carries seven more rows with a witness that is falsifiable against the mechanism it names: three source mutations (dropping the check dedup in `intersect`, dropping the member's annotation merge, and making `value_fits_kind` admit nothing) each turn it red in an isolated worktree at that commit. Rows 1741, 1758, 2400, 2605, 2612, 2619, 2626.

Commit 7e44c5f stages the whole carried-but-unlanded backlog in `conformance/queued-ledger-edits.tsv` (23 Schema.test.ts rows plus these 7), and `python3 conformance/flip-row.py --from-queue conformance/queued-ledger-edits.tsv` lands all thirty in one call. Its `--check` mode verifies the queue without writing; it was run against the live ledger and left the file's sha unchanged.

If you are landing a batch on the tsv, please include that one command. Otherwise drop the tsv lease and I will land it myself.

comments.text:
Batch 1 landed: thirty queued rows are in the ledger, and the tsv lease is free again.

The sibling's exclusive lease on conformance/behavior-tests.tsv was released after their commit 6337b3e, so this lane took it, applied the queue, ran the gates, committed, and released. Five commits, in order:

- cde2cb1 — the seven surviving-intersection rows witnessed, with three source mutations proving the witness falsifiable.
- 7e44c5f — the queue staged in conformance/ plus flip-row.py's --from-queue and --check.
- 8ea093f — the thirty rows flipped.
- d5d9626 — the queue emptied.
- and the defect handoff on this bead plus mail to captain.

## What the thirty were

Thirteen newly carried in Schema.test.ts, seven carrying the allOf intersections in fromJsonSchemaDocument.test.ts, ten RE-POINTS of rows that were already `ported` while citing the wrong witness, and eight excusals of rows whose bodies assert nothing at runtime. The ten re-points are the part worth keeping: the unported count does not move for them, so nothing in the reporting shows they were wrong, but the evidence does change. 8994 cited a Struct-pick test 8664 lines from its sibling; 10559 cited one require() where the mechanism is mapFields over every key.

## Gates, measured

- `cargo test -p elm-effect-schema` exits 0, 22 targets, 0 failures, 132 in schema_corpus.
- `cargo test -p elm-effect-conformance --test ledger` passes ledger_is_well_formed and matched_modules_have_no_unported_behaviors (the third test is ignored by phase).
- rows-port-remaining.py: fromJsonSchemaDocument 84 of 204 (was 91), Schema.test.ts 339 of 606 (was 352).
- The flip touched exactly 30 rows: `git diff -U0` on the committed tsv shows 60 changed lines, each row appearing as one minus/plus pair, nothing else in the file moved.

## Still owed on this lane

The four defects in the handoff comment are unfixed and all four are in src/lib.rs: the `intersect` guard that reads a same-type intersection as a different base (about thirteen rows), the missing `never` answer for incompatible types and contradictions (about seven rows, one of which currently returns a literal instead of refusing), `new_kinded`'s identity decoder for every kind but String, Number and Boolean (silent wrongness on rows already marked ported), and the annotation allow-list that drops contentEncoding, contentMediaType and contentSchema (two rows). Those sit with whichever lane holds lib.rs next; the lease on it is free now.

comments.author: CoralHarbor
comments.text:
Batches 2 and 3 landed. This bead is now 74 of 204 open, down from 91 at the start of the session, and the remaining 74 are measured below: every one is gated on a feature, not on grinding.

## Batch 2, commit f0ed1ce (five rows)

`intersect` answered `Never` where the pin does, and stopped producing a schema weaker than its own inputs.

- 2570, 2577, 2584, 2591, 2598 carried. Three rules: `never` swallows, two members naming different JSON Schema types hold nothing, and two sets of exact values intersect.
- The silent one was the exact-value rule. `{ allOf: [{ const: 1 }, { enum: [1, 2] }] }` admitted 2, because the member's whole enum was kept and the base's own value was never consulted. `{ const: 1 }` beside `{ const: 2 }` gave `Schema.Literal(2)`.
- Same-type-different-shape still refuses on purpose. Answering `Never` there would be worse than saying so.
- The witness asserts the code, the type, AND that the decoder refuses each of the six shapes the members named. `never` that admits a value is exactly what the code string cannot see.
- The witness was red first, on the old refusal, and each of the three rules reverted in turn turns it red again.

## Batch 3, commit 138aa75 (five rows)

A whole class of silent wrongness removed: the import ignored `$dynamicRef`, `contains`, `dependentRequired`, `dependentSchemas`, `unevaluatedItems`, `unevaluatedProperties` and a live `if`/`then`/`else`, returning the open JSON value. A dropped constraint and an enforced one are indistinguishable to whoever wrote the document.

- 1684, 3012, 3035, 3046, 3058 carried. Each keyword is refused by name with the pin's sentence; `not` with a non-empty operand says the same instead of refusing in this port's own words only.
- The other half of :3058 is that these keywords are still ignored when they apply to nothing (`if`/`then`/`else` set to `false`, `minContains`/`maxContains` alone). Refusing those would reject documents the pin accepts, so the conditional check reads the value and the two cardinalities are absent from the table on purpose.
- :3035 is one ledger row over six keywords, so the witness runs all six; the list is the assertion.
- Three mutations revert the table, the conditional rule and the `not` message, and each turns the witness red.

## One suspicion checked and dismissed

The port applies `pattern` by default, where the pin's `fromJsonSchemaDocument` refuses a pattern unless given `patterns: "apply"`. That looked like it made two already-`ported` rows wrong. It does not: the pin's own `assertFromJsonSchema` helper is defined at line 18 as `fromJsonSchemaDocument(document, { patterns: "apply", ...options })`, so every row routed through it applies patterns. Rows :106 and :119 are sound, and the port's single behavior matches the helper. What the port lacks is the option itself, which is what gates 3084, 3099, 3120, 3129 and 3138.

## What the remaining 74 are gated on, measured

- 29 rows on `$ref`/`$defs` with resource scoping: 903, 937, 1168, 1199, 1221, 1256, 1274, 1298, 1305, 1318, 1325, 1344, 1360, 1376, 1397, 1419, 1442, 1466, 1508, 1542, 1560, 1648, 1710, 1726, 2633, 2652, 2669, 2687, 2805. The port refuses every `$ref` with one message, so the refusal rows among these cannot be carried without the feature: a refusal for a coarser reason than the row's would make 1298 read as though references work.
- 16 rows on merging two shapes of the SAME type, which is defect A in the handoff: 2420, 2443, 2461, 2479, 2497, 2515, 2532, 2547 (two arrays), and 2716, 2738, 2758, 2779, 2795, 2817, 2980, 2995 (two objects). Both need an intermediate shape (prefix list, rest, property set, additionalProperties scope) rather than the bare `SchemaKind` the port intersects today. This is the largest single lever left and the one worth scheduling.
- 17 rows on the `patterns` and `onEnter` import options: 2836, 2852, 2872, 2884, 2900, 2918, 2940, 2959, 3084, 3099, 3120, 3129, 3138, 3172, 3195, 3220, 3248.
- 6 rows on pruning a union lane against a constraining sibling: 1585, 1598, 1623, 1648, 1696, 1776.
- 3 rows on `ParseOptions` carrying `onExcessProperty: "error"`: 729, 748, 766.
- 2 rows on an annotation whose value is JSON rather than text, so `contentSchema` can ride along: 1147, 2700. The annotation pairs are `Vec<(String, String)>` throughout, and rendering the nested object the way the pin prints it needs a value that can hold JSON, which is why this is not the one-line allow-list edit it looks like.
- 1 row on representation persistence: 806, and the port has no `toRepresentation`/`fromRepresentation` at all.
- 1 row on a closed patterned record with more than one pattern: 1010.

## Still open from the handoff, in src/lib.rs

Defects A (the same-type merge, 16 rows above) and C (`new_kinded` giving every kind but String, Number and Boolean an identity decoder, which makes a merged intersection claim a repr it does not enforce, including on rows already marked `ported`) are unfixed. C is the serious one and does not show up in any count. The lease on lib.rs is released as of this comment.

title: Port HttpEffect's 22 open behavior rows
description:
Port HttpEffect's 22 open behavior rows from the Effect v4.0.0 pin.

The Rust surface for this file already exists (3 of 25 behavior rows
are `ported`), so this is incremental: carry the remaining rows, do not rebuild
what passes.

## What to read

- The TypeScript at the pin: `~/.cache/effect-4.0.0/packages/effect/testpackages/effect/test/http/HttpEffect.test.ts`
  (and the module under `packages/effect/src/` that it exercises).
- The live row list, which is the spec:

      python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/http/HttpEffect.test.ts

## Rules from the elm-effect skill's port-module reference

- Carry a row only when its behavior is representable in Rust. A carried `it.each`
  row runs every tuple in its table. A test that only asserts the function exists
  does not port the row.
- A row we will not carry is `not-applicable` with a reason in the `rust` column.
  Do not mass-excuse: the ledger's own history calls a run that excused all 6940
  open rows "parity theater", and `matched` is derived, so an excused row cannot
  quietly buy parity.
- `Equal` for domain values treats NaN as equal; `f64`'s `==` stays IEEE.
- Waits go through `Clock`. A direct `tokio::time::sleep` inside the module is a bug.
- Set a row to `ported` only after its Rust test was red and then green, and put
  that test's path in the `rust` column. A `ported` row with an empty `rust`
  column fails `cargo test -p elm-effect-conformance --test ledger`.
- Flip the ledger under a lease: `toron reserve acquire`, edit
  `conformance/behavior-tests.tsv`, commit, release. Never hold the lease between
  batches.

## Done

`cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable` passes and `conformance/rows-port-remaining.py` reports
zero open rows for this file.

close_reason:
closed: all 4 rows of packages/effect/test/http/HttpServer.test.ts are ported. commit 59a3c074d45e546cc8a667dce1b3985a14348840; verdict unit-test-verified; ran `sh -c "cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable && python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/http/HttpServer.test.ts"` => "all 4 rows ported or excused" exit 0; receipt .flywheel/receipts/elm-effect-rs-port-httpserver-cpe0-59a3c074d.unit-test-verified.txt.

Red first: the witness imports test_client_origin, which did not exist, so the test file failed to compile (E0432) before the carrier landed. The last open row (:55) is the scoped-IPv6 refusal: NetAddress::to_url already rejects scope_id != 0 with the address as the error input, and the new test_client_origin is the HttpServer carrier that makes that refusal observable from the test-client surface instead of formatting the address with its scope dropped. Gate name: this bead's fence is `sh -c "..."` with no explicit timeout, so it sits in the non-runnable band and its legal gates are {unit-test-verified, live-verified, worker-receipt, triage-verified}; unit-test-verified is the honest one, since the fence's own cargo half is what proved the row.

PRINCIPLES: sequence-verifiable-units — the row was flipped only after its own Rust test was red then green, and the file now reports all 4 rows ported; subtract-before-you-add — the carrier is one function over the existing NetAddress::to_url rejection rather than a second scope check or a new address type.

title: Port JsonSchema's 122 open behavior rows
description: packages/effect/src/JsonSchema.ts is the dialect-conversion surface: fromSchemaDraft07 / fromSchemaDraft2020_12 / fromSchemaOpenApi3_1 / fromSchemaOpenApi3_0, toDocumentDraft07 / toDocumentDraft04, toMultiDocumentOpenApi3_1, plus rewriteRefs / getReferenceKey / sanitizeOpenApiComponentsSchemasKey. Its 122 open rows in test/JsonSchema.test.ts are the biggest unowned block that is self-contained: the whole module works on plain JSON values, so it needs no AST and no representation layer, and it is the foundation toJsonSchemaDocument (184 open rows) needs for ref rewriting. modules.toml already carries the row (packages/effect/src/JsonSchema.ts, status unmatched). Plan: port the converter engine (URL resolution, resource scopes, location keys, reference relocation) and the five adapters into crates/elm-effect/src/json_schema.rs, reusing the existing json_pointer helpers, with witnesses in crates/elm-effect/tests/port_json_schema.rs. Rows the JS object model owns stay unported with a per-row reason rather than excused.
acceptance_criteria: Every flipped row has a Rust test that was red then green; the dialect URIs, ref relocation and collision refusals match the pin; unsupported rows are not-applicable with a per-row reason.
close_reason: done: 122 of 122 JsonSchema rows ported, 1 of them not-applicable. Work commits c407ad0 (the :156 witness) and ed9eff3 (the ledger line that points at it); verdict unit-test-verified. Ran "timeout 900 cargo test -p elm-effect --test port_json_schema && python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/JsonSchema.test.ts" => 122 passed, 0 failed; all 122 rows ported or excused. Also ran "cargo test -p elm-effect-conformance --test ledger" => 2 passed, 0 failed. Deviations: :2417 stays not-applicable, because the row needs Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument and the port has not built it (the landing commit 4e3746c recorded the excuse; this lane agrees the reason is true, but the row is blocked rather than inapplicable and should be re-witnessed when the emitter lands). :156 was landed by 4e3746c against another row's witness and is corrected in ed9eff3. No behaviour test was weakened to reach this close. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — a row flips only against a test that went red then green, which is what made the wrong witness visible. sequence-verifiable-units — the module was carried in five landable slices rather than one unverifiable drop.

The file header's claim that ajv rows witness shape only is now narrower than the file: those two carry semantics.

My acquire returned granted:[] with a conflict, but the command exits 0 on refusal and I had chained the flip with &&, so it ran. I had 30 of his uncommitted rows in the file. Three mutations of that adapter (stop applying the sanitized key map to refs, treat every schema as a non-resource root, stop refusing OpenAPI-activated keywords) each turn the matching rows red, then the adapter is restored byte-identical (sha1 52388da6d655a7150668adfccd7e503d7aa16bdd).

Ledger state: 106 of 122 committed ported (84 + 22 draft-04). The 14 slice-3 rows are carried and witnessed but sit in conformance/queued-ledger-edits.tsv, because the ledger file is another lane own right now. comments.author: CalmHarbor
comments.text:
SLICE 4: :156 witnessed, commit c407ad0. Every row in this module is now either witnessed or blocked on something outside it.

:156 asserts an ajv equivalence (lift a Draft-07 schema, then compare two validators over six instances). The test-local `accepts` reader the draft-04 rows already used grew `const`, `dependencies` / `dependentRequired` / `dependentSchemas`, `contains` and `if`/`then`/`else`, and a new `canonical_schema` builds the standalone schema the pin hands its 2020-12 validator. The source side of the six-case table is checked against Draft-07's own verdicts, never against the canonical side, so the comparison is not one reader agreeing with itself. Red-witnessed twice: stop lowering `dependencies` and the canonical shape fails; make the reader ignore `const` and the source verdict for `{kind:"compact",values:[1]}` fails. 122 of 122 port_json_schema tests green, and crates/elm-effect/src/json_schema.rs is back at its committed sha 52388da6.

LEDGER, and a defect in it. The tsv working copy carries 15 of my rows uncommitted (the 14 slice-3 rows flipped by the lease holder plus :156), and :156 is set to `ported` against `draft07_preserves_semantics_and_opaque_custom_keywords`, which is the witness for :125, not for :156. c407ad0 puts the correct row in conformance/queued-ledger-edits.tsv, and `flip-row.py --from-queue` rewrites that cell in one call. Mailed to captain at 06:20Z with the exact command.

Also in that working copy: :2417 is `not-applicable`. I disagree. The row is blocked, not inapplicable: the excuse reason is accurate (no `Schema.toJsonSchemaDocument` to hand `to_document_draft04`), but that is a missing emitter, not a row this port will not carry. 148f5e7 landed the Reference repr this hour and that lane is still building the emitter, so the row is one merge from witnessable. Checked today: the schema crate still has no document-shaped emitter. `flip-row.py` has no `unported` status, so un-excusing needs the lease holder or a tool change.

BLOCKED, still: :156 lands with the lease, and :2417 needs the emitter. Nothing else in this lane is mine to take.

title: Port Schema.toEquivalence (toEquivalence.test.ts, 48 rows)
description:
Port Schema.toEquivalence (packages/effect/test/schema/toEquivalence.test.ts, 48 rows) from the Effect v4.0.0 pin.

The pin derives one equivalence relation per AST node behind a `memoize`. This port
installes the relation on the `Schema<T>` value while the schema is built
(`equivalence: Option<Equivalence<T>>`, beside `formatter`), and `to_equivalence` is then a
lookup. A constructor that installs none compares the two values' wire forms.

Carry (26), witnessed by crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_equivalence.rs:
- :25 Never — the pin's `Equivalence.strictEqual` (`===`), so two distinct objects are not
  equivalent even when structurally equal.
- :33/:41/:47/:53/:60/:69 tuple shapes, :81 Array, :148/:154/:162/:192/:205 Struct,
  :221 Class, :236/:254 Record, :469 Date, :293/:323/:339 suspend — the existing constructors'
  relations already answer these, so the rows witness them without new code.
- :293 + :421 — the `derivations` counts: an `overrideToEquivalence` factory runs once while
  the schema is built, so a Union member's relation is derived once and the recursive body is
  reused per depth rather than re-derived.
- :456 union member relations and :499 Option's value relation — the two rows that needed new
  code: `union_with_mode` now selects the member whose own decode accepts both values and
  answers with that member's relation; `Schema<Option<T>>::optional` now applies the value
  schema's relation on the `Some` side.
- :647/:655/:663 `overrideToEquivalence`, including one that replaces a compiler-owned
  relation (`Option`'s).

Excuse (22), each with its own reason:
- :90/:104/:123/:135 `TupleWithRest` rest lists: the port's `tuple_with_rest` takes ONE rest
  schema where the pin takes a list of trailing elements (documented in
  crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_core.rs:771).
- :173 symbol keys, :261 `Record(Symbol, Number)`: `Unknown` has no symbol property key.
- :246 `Record(String, UndefinedOr(Number))`: the port has no `UndefinedOr`; its nearest
  spelling (`Option`) is a different declaration whose value type is `Option<T>`, not
  `T | undefined`.
- :440 `selects transformed Union members on the Type side`: the pin's `decodeTo(Target, ...)`
  carries the target's relation; the port's `convert` takes no target schema and its union has
  no Type-side member selection.
- :476 URL, :483 RegExp, :492 Redacted, :512 Result, :526 ReadonlySet, :540 ReadonlyMap,
  :556 HashMap, :572 Duration, :586 BigDecimal, :594 DateTimeUtc, :605 TimeZoneOffset,
  :615 TimeZoneNamed, :625 TimeZone, :635 DateTimeZoned: the port has no schema for any of
  those types, so there is no typed side to relate.

Done: `cargo test -p elm-effect-schema --test schema_equivalence` passes (26 tests) and
`rows-port-remaining.py` reports zero open rows for this file.

CARRIED THIS BATCH (10 rows), witnessed in crates/elm-effect-schema/tests/schema_codec.rs:
  :585/:596/:607  Literal(string|number|boolean) round-trips; nothing else decodes
  :642/:653      TemplateLiteral([1n, String]) and (["a", BigInt]): parse takes the

                 identity on it (and a1.2 / b1 do not match)
  :893          Array(Date): each element travels as its ISO-8601 UTC text
  :905/:918     NullOr(String) and NullOr(Number): the member and null both travel
  :931          Array(NullOr(Number))

CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS COMMENT'S READING, which changes this bead's scope:
TestSchema.Asserts is NOT an AST-comparison harness. Its surface is
  asserts.encoding().succeed(value, encoded?)     -> encode(value) must give encoded
  asserts.decoding().succeed(encoded, value?)     -> decode(encoded) must give value
  asserts.decoding().fail(encoded, message)       -> decode(encoded) must fail with that text
That is a codec round-trip harness, and it maps directly onto the port's
decode/encode plus the error vocabulary, so the ~150 Asserts rows are carryable
against Schema<T>::decode / (try_)encode rather than needing a Schema.Assert
equivalent or a mass excuse. The AST-identity sub-family is the real exception:
:40, :57, :73, :90, :103, :115, :147, :216, :222, :344, :353 and friends assert
serializer.ast / SchemaAST.getLastEncoding / context flags on the AST object.

either a repr-level witness (repr_kind / to_code / to_type already exist) or an
explicit excuse decision. That decision belongs to the operator, not to a
row-flipping batch.

total over Unknown (no path for the refusal to reach the caller), and only went
green once the schema bead's "give encode a failure channel" change landed

title: race_all_first is flaky and fails roughly one run in three, breaking every port bead's cargo test -p fence
description:
`race_all_first_completes_on_the_first_completion_even_a_failure` fails
about one run in three. It timed out at 10s on the failing run and passed in
0.00s on the others, so the failure is a wait that never completed rather than
a wrong value.

Reproduced 2026-10-11 on the current tree:

    for i in 1 2 3; do cargo test -p elm-effect --test race race_all_first; done
    run1: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 0.00s
    run2: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 0.00s
    run3: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; ... finished in 10.00s

Three runs are enough to call it flaky and not enough to call it a
one-off. I did NOT rerun it until it went green: Rule 1.0 forbids treating a
rerun-until-pass as a pass, so this is filed rather than worked around.

## Why it matters here specifically

`cargo test -p elm-effect` is the fence for every port bead's VERIFY, and
`sh conformance/behavior-tests.tsv`'s port columns are flipped against a green
run. A suite that is green roughly two times in three means any bead's fence
can fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the bead, and the honest
response is to run the fence repeatedly and record which failure belongs to
the port. That is exactly the cost this bead removes.

It also surfaced mid-session while closing `elm-effect-rs-port-cause-qii`, whose
own tests (`l2_cause`, 73 cases) are deterministic and green every time. The
failure was in `race.rs`, a file that port did not touch.

## What lands

- A deterministic `race_all_first` case: drive the two sides through the
  runtime's own scheduling rather than a wall-clock race, or bound the wait so
  a stalled side fails with a named timeout instead of hanging to the harness
  limit.
- The test must not pass by making the race trivially ordered if the point of
  the row is that the loser is interrupted; the ported behavior row
  `race_all_first_completes_on_the_first_completion_even_a_failure` asserts the
  first COMPLETION wins, so the fix must keep that property under test.
close_reason: status: done; commit aecba71c10e11c30d240d7f73457bb927dc4d23c; verdict unit-test-verified; ran the bead VERIFY (5x loop of cargo test -p elm-effect --test race race_all_first) => exit 0, 5/5 green; plus 8/8 green on the same filter and cargo test -p elm-effect exit 0 for the whole crate. Pre-fix control: 6 runs failed on run 6 after exactly 10.00s (wait_until deadline), matching the filed report. Evidence .flywheel/receipts/elm-effect-rs-race-all-first-flaky-o83c-aecba71c10e11c30d240d7f73457bb927dc4d23c.unit-test-verified.txt. DEVIATION (loud): rewrote the bead's VERIFY comparison. BSD wc -l pads its count ('       0'), so '| wc -l | grep -qx 0' could never match on this host even on an all-green run; the assertion is unchanged (zero failures in 5 runs), only the arithmetic is now portable. The same broken shape still sits in elm-effect-rs-uqh's fence. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — the flake was reproduced before the fix and the fix was re-run 8/8 through the unwrapped cargo, not a self-report; fix-root-causes — synchronized the race inside race_all_first's own bodies instead of lengthening wait_until's deadline.

title: Schema: ArrayEnsure decodes one value or an array
description: Schema.test.ts :1210 (ArrayEnsure), :1232 (roundtrips array-valued elements) and :1239 (preserves outer-array encoding). Schema::array_ensure tries the inner schema first, so a one-element array of an array stays one tuple; an array the inner schema refuses decodes element-wise. Encoding is the inverse: a one-element array unwraps to the single value, every other array encodes element-wise, which is what makes the tuple round trip exact. The pin builds this as Union([one, many]) over a decodeTo; the port keeps only the order the union tries, and a value neither member accepts reports the inner schema's refusal rather than the union's joined type text.
close_reason: done

title: Schema: a check reads the value its transform produced
description: Schema.test.ts :2880 (Redacted(Finite)), :2917 (Redacted(FiniteFromString)) and :3008 (RedactedFromValue should decode a value). The pin's check lands on the target side of a link, so FiniteFromString.check(isInt()) refuses "1.2" by reading the number the transform produced. Adds check_view to Schema: a wire-to-target projection set by the typed transforms (finite/number from string), propagated through annotate, as_unknown, checked and the filter group, and applied by check_value on both axes. Failures now carry TypeMismatchDynamic, so SchemaError::at and the field/array path rewrites name the variant too (a check on a field reports at that field). A box validates what it holds on the way out, not only on the way in. :2662 and :2791 stay unported: as_unknown normalizes a typed transform back to wire form, so a flip of it produces no typed value, and the port has no decodeTo link.

title: Schema.Enum: the five Enum rows (finite guard, names, numeric/string/const)
description: Schema.test.ts Enum rows :7810 (rejects non-finite numeric values), :7819 (enums should be exposed), :7829 (Numeric enum), :7853 (String enum), :7881 (Const enum). The pin takes a TypeScript enum or a const object; here the names arrive as pairs, so Schema::enumeration keeps them in declaration order and exposes them, and the codec is a real union of literals. The union must be union_with_mode, not the two-member Schema::union chain, or the refusal loses the pin's own 'Expected 0 | 1' text. A non-finite numeric member panics at build time with the pin's message, because such a member is unreachable on the wire.

title: Schema.flip: the swapped codec and the five rows that need it
description: Schema.test.ts :2654 (a flip exposes the schema), :2684/:2710/:2736/:2762 (Struct/Tuple/Union/Declaration flip & check & flip applies the check to the encoded side) and :9049 (Union options survive public derivations). Schema::flip swaps the two directions of a codec at the Unknown level: decode becomes try_encode and encode becomes decode. The shape underneath is kept through the wrapped reprs, so a flipped Union is still a Union whose options a derivation reads, and flip_source reads the schema back. The pin splits checks into a from-side list and encodingChecks and a flip moves one into the other; this port's filter chain runs on both axes of whatever carries it, so flip & check & flip needs no such split and the witness asserts the behaviour the split produces. :2662 and :2791 stay unported: both need a check to read a value the codec produced (a transformed output, or a link's local value), which this port's checks cannot do.

title: Port Command's 98 open behavior rows
description:
Port packages/effect/test/cli/Command.test.ts from the Effect v4.0.0 pin. 98 rows
are unported and none is ported yet, so this is a new surface rather than an
incremental one. No bead owned this file before.

## What exists already

The Rust surface is split across two files and is NOT a Command implementation:

- crates/elm-effect-unstable/src/cli_ai.rs:100 — `pub struct Command`
- crates/elm-effect-unstable/src/cli.rs:45 — `pub struct CommandRoute`

Read both first and decide whether the rows extend them or need a new module. Do
not rebuild what already passes.

## What to read

- The TypeScript at the pin:
  ~/.cache/effect-4.0.0/packages/effect/test/cli/Command.test.ts
- The module it exercises under packages/effect/src/cli/ (Command.ts and its
  Wizard surface).
- The live row list, which is the spec:

      python3 conformance/rows-port-remaining.py packages/effect/test/cli/Command.test.ts

## What the rows actually need

Every open row in this file is it.effect. The families are:

- help-doc annotation exposure, and annotations surviving subcommand addition
  (:51, :81)
- the wizard invoked programmatically from a command handler, and
  wizard-generated arguments run with --wizard (:119, :142)
- negative numbers parsed as flag and argument values, and negative integer
  flag values through --wizard (:168, :182)
- round-tripping a wizard flag value, including mixed repeated values (:211, :229)
- redaction of option-looking values in wizard command output (:252)
- boolean wizard values rendered consistently (:301)
- wizard mode starting at a selected subcommand (:320)
- --completions rejected without a shell, and --name rejected without an
  expected value (:339, :370)
- invalid choice values rendered without doubling the "Expected" prefix (:388)

So the core to build first is a flag parser that treats a leading '-' as a value
as well as a flag, and a small wizard that walks named choices and produces an
argument list. Build only what the earliest rows exercise and carry what that
unlocks.

## Rules

- cargo test -p elm-effect-unstable must stay green per chunk.
- Run `timeout 600 cargo build` before EVERY commit. A pre-commit build gate now
  refuses a commit whose staged packages do not build, and an unbuilt tree blocks
  every other crew.
- Commits cite ONLY this bead id. One bead id per commit message.
- DO NOT touch anything under crates/elm-effect-schema/ — three crews hold it and
  you would collide.
- If a row cannot be represented yet, excuse it with a one-line reason naming the
  specific missing API and its file/line. Never bulk-excuse.
- Report carried/excused counts every ~20 rows.

title: snapshot_runs: sweep project logs through state::project_logs()
description:
`snapshot_runs()` hand-rolls the state-dir `*.jsonl` sweep instead of using
`project_logs()`, so reserved non-project logs are parsed as project logs and
every row is dropped as malformed.

`src/main.rs:3636-3656` does `read_dir` + `trim_end_matches(".jsonl")` with no
`RESERVED_NON_PROJECT_LOGS` filter, while the documented one-enumeration helper
exists at `src/state.rs:1263-1286`. The identical bug was already fixed in
`workflow history` — `src/main.rs:30083-30089` carries a comment describing
this exact failure.

Reproduced: `flywheel --robot-status 2>/tmp/e >/dev/null; grep -c "skipping
malformed log line" /tmp/e` prints **20**, one per row of `miss-ledger.jsonl`,
all `missing field 'kind'` (the reserved-log schema).

Cosmetic — stdout JSON is unaffected and every agent driver discards stderr —
but it is 20 lines of noise on the single command agents run most, and it

title: Fiber: interruption reaches the whole subtree when it is requested
description: FiberHandle::interrupt set only the target's flag; children were interrupted at the end of the target's own body. A body blocked joining its own child therefore deadlocked: runtime::timeout forks the body, interrupts it on the deadline, and waits, while the body waits for a child nobody stopped. Fix: Shared::interrupt_tree walks descendants depth first, firing each deferred child's start latch before requesting the interrupt, from both interrupt and interrupt_unsafe. Witness: a parent that blocks in child.join(); without recursive delivery the child parks forever and the witness aborts at its watchdog.

title: 90 test files with open behavior rows are linked to no module row, freezing the phase-13 gate and letting a bead get the wrong crate
description:
90 of the 223 test files that carry open behavior rows are linked to no module
row in conformance/modules.toml. A run of conformance/inventory.sh leaves them
that way, so this is not hand-editing drift.

## What it breaks

The module row's `tests` list is the only thing that tells the rest of the
conformance tooling which test file belongs to which source module. With no
link:

1. `inventory.sh` derives `matched`/`unmatched` from "port-like and has linked
   behavior rows", so an unlinked test file's module stays `unmatched` no matter
   how many of its rows get ported. `matched_modules_have_no_unported_
   behaviors` and `port_rows_are_matched` (the phase-13 gate) both read that
   status, so the gate cannot move for those files.

2. `make-port-backlog.py` resolves a bead's crate from the module row's class,
   and falls back to `elm-effect` when the row links no test. For the FindMyWay
   tests that is wrong: the router lives in elm-effect-unstable, so a bead
   written `cargo test -p elm-effect` is green regardless of whether the port
   is right — a vacuous fence, which is worse than a broken one.

## Where it shows up

Found while closing `elm-effect-rs-port-querystring-uinz` and
`elm-effect-rs-port-case-insensitive-8civ`. Both were generated with
`cargo test -p ?` (fixed in a separate commit). Hand-correcting them to
`elm-effect-unstable` is what forced the question of why the generator could
not know that on its own, and the answer is the empty `tests` list.

The unlinked files include HttpClient.test.ts, StackCapture.test.ts, all of the
ai/ representation and Mcp conformance tests, and the FindMyWay family.

## Why this is worth a bead and not a one-line fix

The linking rule lives in inventory.sh's test-matching pass. It matches a test
path to a module path by pattern, and it deliberately skips what it cannot prove
(rather than guessing), which is the right default — but the result is 90 files
with no home. Two of them already cost a wrong crate on a generated bead, and
the rest cost a gate that cannot move. The owner has to decide the matching
rule for these families, and that decision is a policy call, not a bugfix.

comments.author: bangedorrunt
comments.text:
Measured root cause (CalmHarbor). The matcher cannot be widened on the evidence available; this is a ledger policy call, and here is the data to make it on.

COUNTS at this pin (10-12): 377 module rows; 340 test files have behavior rows; 214 have OPEN (unported) rows; 88 of those 214 are linked to no module row, carrying 1983 open rows. (The bead says 90; the ledger has moved since.)

FAMILIES: schema 41 files / 1266 rows, ai 24 / 365, cli 6 / 152, top-level 4 / 80, http 4 / 66, arbitrary 3 / 21, httpapi 2 / 19, eventlog 2 / 8, cluster 1 / 4, observability 1 / 2.

THREE FACTS that kill the obvious fixes:
1. The test's file name is not evidence of its module. 85 of 88 have no module row at the path their name predicts, and where a row exists the names disagree anyway: test/cli/Arguments.test.ts (plural) against row packages/effect/src/cli/Argument.ts (singular). The cli inventory itself is complete (13 non-internal source files at the pin, 13 rows), so this is a naming gap, not a missing row.
2. No import names a source module. 0 of 88 import anything matching /src/. 46 import only test helpers (../TestUtils/..., ./McpConformance.ts) and 42 import only package barrels (effect, effect/testing, @effect/vitest). So an import-reading rule links test files to helpers, never to modules.
3. The barrel route needs symbol resolution, and it has targets. The barrel-only files name their subject as a SYMBOL: test/schema/* uses Schema (23x), SchemaParser (10x), SchemaGetter (10x), SchemaTransformation, SchemaJITCompiler, VariantSchema. Rows exist for src/Schema.ts, src/schema/SchemaJITCompiler.ts, src/schema/VariantSchema.ts, plus 139 top-level src module rows. Resolving symbol -> defining module means reading the barrel's re-export map, which inventory.sh does not do today.

THE THREE OPTIONS, with what each buys and costs:
a) Symbol resolution in inventory.sh: derive each test file's subject from the barrel's re-export map. Provable, not guessed, but it is new machinery in the generator and it will relink many already-linked files, so it must be checked as a red-then-green script like the earlier rounds (see docs/learnings/inbox/2026-10-10-conformance-linking-and-loop-dispatch.md).
b) Declare package-level tests: link a barrel-only test file to the module whose name the package gives it (test/schema/toCodec.test.ts -> src/toCodec.ts if that row exists) and leave nothing else linked. Cheap, but it links only the subset whose name does match a row; the Schema.test.ts family stays unlinked.
c) Exclude package-level test files from the matched/unmatched derivation: the phase-13 gate would then read them as package conformance rather than module conformance. This is the honest reading of what these files are, and it is the option that most changes gate semantics, so it needs the clearest sign-off.

Measured counterexample to watch under (a): src/cli has 13 rows, so if a wider rule links Arguments.test.ts to Argument.ts by name, the link is a rename guess, not proof.
