title: Let a static Interpreter reach the world its loop was booted with
description:
An Interpret is static: interpret(cmd) -> Effect<Msg, Err> has no parameters a host could use to hand it the world. So use_service inside one was a dead end, and a runtime built by ManagedRuntime::make had its services read back by context() for tests and never consulted at a run.

Found porting beads (beads_rust-04yf9): a CLI over a rusqlite store that is RefCell-backed and !Sync cannot put the store in an Effect at all, and cannot use Loop either, because neither Send bounds nor the static trait give it a door.

## What lands

- Effect::provide_from(&BuiltServices) -> Effect<A, E, Rest>: closes tag T out of a runtime's built services instead of out of a value in hand. Fail-closed: a tag the layer never built is missing service: <id> at the run edge, never a default.
- Effect::map_err(f): translates the typed failure channel via the existing Cause::map, so use_service (Infallible) can join the Err a Program declares. Defects and interrupts pass through untouched.
- Interpret::interpret_in_env(cmd, Option<&BuiltServices>) with a default that ignores them and calls interpret, so every existing interpreter keeps working unchanged.
- Loop::run_window passes self.rt.context() into interpret_in_env.

## Fence note
cargo clippy -p elm-effect -p elm-effect-elm --all-targets -D warnings cannot pass on main: 89 pre-existing findings in foundation.rs (method not) and stream.rs (very complex type, x2), none of them in a file this change touches. The fence pins the count instead, and comm proves the set is byte-identical with and without the patch, so this change adds none.

## Not in this slice
Nothing about Send. Effect::sync and ManagedRuntime::run keep their Send bounds (docs/learnings/inbox/2026-10-04-elm-send-bounds.md records that as a deliberate decision); a !Sync world now enters as a service value, which is Clone + Send + Sync, exactly as 06-services.mdx's 'put a socket in an Arc' instructs.

description:

three classes of defect, all reproduced mechanically (see also the audit script
landed with this bead).

1. **26 malformed rows.** `packages/effect/test/schema/toIso.test.ts` carries a

3. **Unfalsifiable excuses.** 593 rows say "internals not exposed" without
   naming an API, on modules that do exist in the port.

## This bead

- Fix the 26 malformed rows so the file has exactly 6 fields per row.
- Make `Behavior::load` refuse a malformed row, and assert the declared

- Carry the RcMap and RateLimiter rows whose behavior the existing surface

The 222-row Schema blanket needs a per-row re-audit (a port campaign), the 593
vague reasons need per-row engineering or a reason convention, and the
`matched` status has no floor against an excuse-heavy test file (37 modules
would un-match under a `ported > excused` rule; that is a policy call, not a
mechanical fix).

title: Effect: 100k nested map continuations overflow the interpreter stack
description: Row 2713 (lazily nested map continuations) fails today: a 100k-deep defer+map chain aborts with "has overflowed its stack" at the default 8MB stack. Two public gaps and one interpreter shape: (1) Effect.suspend is missing (only a crate-private suspend(ErasedStep, Services)); (2) map/flat_map evaluate `first` with a nested run_sync_with call, so interpreter depth equals nesting depth. ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED (measured): adding Completion::{Done,Tail} so a step hands its continuation back to a run loop fixes only the continuation side; FlatMap still calls first.run_sync_with recursively, and the 100k witness still aborts (SIGABRT). The whole suite stayed green with the change, so it is safe but insufficient. The fix that actually works needs a shared continuation stack: either type-erase step values (Step holds Box<dyn Any + Send>, every combinator downcasts) so one loop owns all frames, or a CPS interpreter where bind pushes a frame instead of recursing. Then add the public suspend, create crates/elm-effect/tests/effect_stack_safety.rs with the 100_000 witness, and flip row 2713.

description: Rows 54 and 103 (and the defect/concurrency rows 8, 32, 188, 551) remain. Row 281 was carried separately by retiring referenced entries on invalidation. For 54/103 the gap is per-entry idle-fiber state: the pin releases row 54 at ref drop because no timer was armed before the invalidation, while row 103 waits for a timer armed before the re-acquire; a key-level idle clock cannot encode both. title: Link the 22 port modules whose test inventory.sh's key derivation and name filter miss
description:
**Corrected premise.** This bead first claimed "no checkout of effect@4.0.0 exists on this machine". False: `~/.cache/effect-4.0.0` is a checkout of tag `effect@4.0.0` at commit `67ba4e4`, already documented in `docs/plan/bead-briefs.md`. Nothing needed vendoring.

## Two bugs, one cause

`inventory.sh` could not see 22 port modules' tests, so they read `tests = []` and `port_like_unmatched()` counted them forever. The phase-13 gate reported **296** unmatched; of those, **164** could never match however many behavior rows got ported.

**1. Key derivation.** The link key strips `packages/effect/src/` and `packages/effect/test/` independently, so a module and its test only meet when they share a subdirectory. Missed 20: `Schema`, `SchemaAST`, `SchemaParser`, `SchemaGetter`, `SchemaIssue`, `SchemaRepresentation` (→ `http/`), `SchemaTransformation`, `Arbitrary`, `ai/McpProtocol`, `ai/McpServer`, the seven `http-api/*` (test dir is `httpapi/`), `reactivity/AtomRef`, `sql/Migrator`, `testing/TestClock`.

**2. Name filter.** The link scanner ran `find -name '*.test.ts'`, but the persistence and MCP-conformance suites name files `FooTest.ts`. The behavior scanner reads every `.ts`, so those rows were always witnessed — only the link was blind. Missed 2: `process/ChildProcessSpawner`, `persistence/RateLimiter` (plus second links for `KeyValueStore`, `PersistedCache`, `PersistedQueue`, which have both `Foo.test.ts` and `FooTest.ts`).

## The fix, and the one trap

The relative key stays primary — `src/ai/Prompt.ts` and `src/cli/Prompt.ts` share a basename and `ledger.rs` asserts each links only its own directory. The basename fallback fires only when the relative key misses, only when the basename is unclaimed, and only when exactly one candidate survives.

The trap: `test/ai/Model.test.ts` belongs to `src/ai/Model.ts` (it imports from `effect/ai`), and a naive basename fallback hands it to `src/schema/Model.ts` too. So the script collects every relative-key claim first and refuses to steal one. `Model` is left unlinked rather than mislinked.

## Verified

- `port_like_unmatched()` 296 → **294**; the never-matchable ceiling 164 → **142**.
- `matched` modules 73 → 75.
- Regenerated `modules.toml`, idempotent (byte-identical across two runs).
- 9970 behavior rows: 0 keys lost or gained, **0** rows had `(status, rust)` move.
- 21 hand-written `reason` notes: 0 lost.
- 0 modules with a non-empty link had it altered; every change is additive.
- `cargo test -p elm-effect-conformance --test ledger` passes.

## Not in this slice

The **142** modules that remain have no test file at the pin at all (`index.ts` barrels, `cluster/*`, `eventlog/*`, `workflow/*`, `rpc/*`, `http/*`, `cli/*` type surfaces). They are a definition question about the gate, reported as a ceiling to the operator; reclassifying them to make `port_like_unmatched()` empty would loosen a gate, which is operator-only.

title: doorbell wake brain saturates and drops 273k watch lines; digests report events the consumer can never replay
description:
The doorbell's wake brain channel saturates and drops watch lines, so
coordination events are silently lost while the digest still reports them as
queued.

`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/flywheel-elm-effect-rs.audit.jsonl` holds
**5462** `wake_brain_full` events totalling **273,296 dropped watch lines**, the
worst single event dropping **513**. The reason string names the mechanism:
`watch line could not be enqueued (brain channel full); reporting one death so
the consumer restarts and replays from the cursor`.

## Why it looked like so many separate bugs

Every digest delivered to the arriving agent this session claimed N queued
events and then read empty, which presented as three unrelated symptoms:

- `toron channel read adr0006-steer` returned `[]` on four separate calls while
  the digest said "1 queued". Not a race — the retry was immediate and returned
  `[]` twice in a row. The kind-9 post was dropped before it reached the bus, so
  the journal had a row the channel could never serve.
- The `[deaf]` digest lines (`subscriber=workspace:flywheel-elm-effect-rs
  attempts=1 unanswered`) were read as a broken prompt wake. The wake brain was
  not broken, it was full.
- The channel was read as "mail-only, not wake", which the flywheel skill's
  rule 11 reinforces. The actual condition was event loss.

## What lands

- Bound the wake brain channel: either a real capacity with a documented drop
  policy and a counter surfaced in `/health`, or a blocking send so the producer
  backpressures instead of shedding.
- `dropped` and `wake_brain_full` counts must appear in `/health` and in
  `flywheel doorbell status`, not only in an audit journal nobody reads. A
  digest that reports "N queued" while the consumer cannot replay them is a
  silent failure, and it must be loud.
- The consumer restart the reason string promises must actually replay from the
  cursor; verify the dropped lines are recovered rather than discarded.

## Note

This host carries seven workspaces on one doorbell daemon
(`~/.local/state/flywheel/doorbell/`), and `flywheel-beads.audit.jsonl` alone is
12,341 lines. Backpressure of this scale may be a capacity problem specific to
a saturated daemon rather than a code defect — but the silent-drop path is the
bug either way, and it is the bug that made this session's coordination plane
look broken in three different ways at once.

title: RcMap: clock-injected TTL, getOption, and the pin's capacity failure
description:
The excuse audit reopened 15 RcMap rows. Ten of them are blocked by three
surface gaps the port can close without a redesign:

- **No clock.** Idle TTL is counted against `std::time::Instant`, so the TTL
  rows (RcMap.test.ts:249, :370, :413, :492, :522) have no virtual-time
  witness. The pin's `idleTimeToLive` is read per key and re-armed on release
  and `touch`.
- **No `getOption`.** :150 asserts a cached-only read that neither looks up nor
  takes capacity. The port has only the acquiring `get`.
- **No capacity failure.** The pin fails a new key with
  `ExceededCapacityError` at `capacity`, and never evicts to make room; the
  port's `evict` silently drops unreferenced entries, which is a different rule
  (:444, :54, :103).

## This bead

Route idle TTL through an injected millisecond clock (declared in the module:
it compiles through `#[path]` includes, so `crate::time` is out of scope), add
`has`, `get_option`, a per-key TTL setter and an `expire_idle` sweep, and give
`get` the pin's capacity failure through a new `RcMapError<E>`. Carry every row
the new surface witnesses.

## Residual

Rows that need a redesign stay open: the defect channel (:8, :32 — a throwing
lookup is not a typed failure here), in-flight sharing with a deferred (:188),
deferred release for an invalidated entry still held (:281), and the
finalizer-on-close race (:551) unless the sweep makes it observable.
close_reason: RcMap grows an injected clock, getOption, has, a per-key TTL, an expire_idle sweep and RcMapError::ExceededCapacity; 8 of the 15 reopened rows are carried with 11 witnesses, 7 stay open with named residuals (defect channel, deferred invalidate, in-flight sharing, close race). Two stdlib tests rewritten to the pin rules.
